021import java.io.*;

023import java.net.URISyntaxException;

033/**
034 * Revision-neutral base class for Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients.
035 *
036 * <p>
037 * Wraps a single configured {@link RestClient} and executes raw JSON-RPC 2.0 request/response round trips against one
038 * endpoint in JSON response mode. A generic {@link RestCallInterceptor} passthrough is provided on the builder so
039 * per-revision facades can layer auth and other cross-cutting concerns without changing this core.
040 *
041 * <p>
042 * {@link #send(JsonRpcRequest)} returns the complete {@link JsonRpcResponse} envelope untouched, including
043 * {@code error} responses - it does not throw {@link McpException} on a JSON-RPC error. Typed facades are
044 * responsible for translating a response with a non-<jk>null</jk> {@link JsonRpcResponse#getError() error} into a
045 * thrown {@link McpException}.
046 *
047 * <p>
048 * Instances are thread-safe for concurrent reuse: {@link RestClient} and endpoint are final, and each
049 * {@link #send(JsonRpcRequest)} creates a fresh request/response scope. Builders are single-use value assemblers:
050 * calling {@code build()} twice creates two clients and both use the same explicitly configured transport instance.
051 *
052 * <p>
053 * <b>Beta - API subject to change:</b> This class builds directly on {@code org.apache.juneau.rest.client}, which
054 * is itself Beta.
055 *
056 * @since 10.0.0
057 */
058@SuppressWarnings({
059   "resource" // The RestClient is built once and held in a field that close() closes.
060})
061public abstract class AbstractMcpClient implements Closeable {
062
063   // JSON-RPC methods that are side-effect-free (pure queries), so a pre-response stale-connection failure can be
064   // safely replayed once.  Kept as revision-neutral protocol literals rather than a dependency on any dated
065   // McpMethods class.  Any method NOT listed here — notably tools/call, subscriptions/listen, sampling/createMessage,
066   // notifications/*, and any unknown method — is never replayed, so a mutating operation can never double-execute.
067   private static final Set<String> RETRYABLE_METHODS = Set.of(
068      "initialize",
069      "server/discover",
070      "ping",
071      "tools/list",
072      "prompts/list",
073      "prompts/get",
074      "resources/list",
075      "resources/read",
076      "resources/templates/list",
077      "completion/complete");
078
079   private final RestClient restClient;
080   private final String endpoint;
081
082   /**
083    * Constructor.
084    *
085    * @param builder The builder supplying this client's configuration. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
086    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If {@code builder} is <jk>null</jk>, or its endpoint is <jk>null</jk>/blank
087    *    or is not a syntactically valid absolute {@code http}/{@code https} URL (see
088    *    {@link #validateEndpoint(String)}).
089    */
090   protected AbstractMcpClient(Builder<?> builder) {
091      reqnn("builder", builder);
092      this.endpoint = validateEndpoint(builder.endpoint);
093      this.restClient = builder.restClientBuilder
094         .defaultSerializer(JsonSerializer.DEFAULT)
095         .defaultParser(JsonParser.DEFAULT)
096         .build();
097   }
098
099   /**
100    * Validates the configured endpoint: non-<jk>null</jk>/non-blank (as before), and additionally that it
101    * parses as a syntactically valid, absolute URL using the {@code http} or {@code https} scheme.
102    *
103    * <p>
104    * Rejecting a malformed or non-http(s) endpoint here, at construction, is preferable to letting it surface
105    * later as an opaque transport failure on the first {@link #send(JsonRpcRequest)} call.
106    *
107    * @param value The candidate endpoint. Must not be <jk>null</jk>/blank.
108    * @return {@code value}, unchanged, once validated.
109    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If {@code value} is <jk>null</jk>/blank, is not a syntactically valid URI,
110    *    has no scheme, or has a scheme other than {@code http}/{@code https} (case-insensitive).
111    */
112   private static String validateEndpoint(String value) {
113      var endpointValue = reqnb("endpoint", value);
114      URI uri;
115      try {
116         uri = new URI(endpointValue);
117      } catch (URISyntaxException e) {
118         throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid MCP endpoint URL '" + endpointValue + "': " + e.getMessage(), e);
119      }
120      var scheme = uri.getScheme();
121      if (scheme == null || ! (eqic(scheme, "http") || eqic(scheme, "https")))
122         throw new IllegalArgumentException(
123            "Invalid MCP endpoint URL '" + endpointValue + "': must be an absolute http or https URL, but scheme was '" + scheme + "'.");
124      return endpointValue;
125   }
126
127   /**
128    * Sends a raw JSON-RPC request and returns the raw JSON-RPC response envelope.
129    *
130    * <p>
131    * A request with a <jk>null</jk> {@link JsonRpcRequest#getId() id} is a notification: this method still sends
132    * it over the wire, but always returns <jk>null</jk> without attempting to read a response body, per the
133    * JSON-RPC 2.0 notification contract (the server sends no response body for a notification).
134    *
135    * @param request The JSON-RPC request to send. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
136    * @return The JSON-RPC response envelope, or <jk>null</jk> if {@code request} is a notification.
137    * @throws IOException If a transport-level or (de)serialization error occurs.
138    */
139   public JsonRpcResponse send(JsonRpcRequest request) throws IOException {
140      return send(request, Map.of());
141   }
142
143   /**
144    * Sends a raw JSON-RPC request and returns the raw JSON-RPC response envelope.
145    *
146    * <p>
147    * A request with a <jk>null</jk> {@link JsonRpcRequest#getId() id} is a notification: this method still sends
148    * it over the wire, but always returns <jk>null</jk> without attempting to read a response body, per the
149    * JSON-RPC 2.0 notification contract (the server sends no response body for a notification).
150    *
151    * <p>
152    * <b>Note:</b> for a notification, this method returns <jk>null</jk> immediately after the transport call
153    * completes, without ever inspecting {@link RestResponse#getStatusCode()}. A non-2xx HTTP status on a
154    * notification is therefore silently swallowed - the caller sees no indication that the server rejected it.
155    * This is intentional per the notification contract above (there is no response envelope to report an error
156    * through), but it does mean transport-level failures on notifications are otherwise invisible to callers.
157    *
158    * @param request The JSON-RPC request to send. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
159    * @param httpHeaders Optional additional HTTP headers to add on this request. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
160    * @return The JSON-RPC response envelope, or <jk>null</jk> if {@code request} is a notification.
161    * @throws IOException If a transport-level or (de)serialization error occurs.
162    */
163   public JsonRpcResponse send(JsonRpcRequest request, Map<String,String> httpHeaders) throws IOException {
164      reqnn("request", request);
165      try (var res = run(request, httpHeaders)) {
166         if (JsonRpcResponse.notification(request.getId()))
167            return null;
168         var sc = res.getStatusCode();
169         JsonRpcResponse parsed;
170         try {
171            parsed = res.body().as(JsonRpcResponse.class);
172         } catch (IOException e) {
173            if (sc < 200 || sc > 299)
174               throw ioex(e, "MCP server returned HTTP %s and the body was not a JSON-RPC envelope.", sc);
175            throw e;
176         }
177         if (parsed == null)
178            throw ioex("No response body received for JSON-RPC request id '%s' (HTTP %s).", request.getId(), sc);
179         return parsed;
180      }
181   }
182
183   /**
184    * Runs the request, transparently retrying exactly once on a pre-response stale-connection failure when the
185    * JSON-RPC method is side-effect-free.
186    *
187    * <p>
188    * Every MCP call is transported as an HTTP {@code POST}, which a transport can never safely replay (a {@code POST}
189    * may have already executed server-side before the connection dropped).  A pooled keep-alive connection can,
190    * however, be torn down by the server between requests, causing the very next reuse to fail with an immediate
191    * {@code EOF} before any response is received.  Keying the replay decision on JSON-RPC method idempotency here —
192    * rather than on the HTTP method — lets such a failure be recovered for a read-only call (e.g.
193    * {@code resources/read}) without risking a duplicate side effect.  Mutating methods (e.g. {@code tools/call}) and
194    * any method not in {@link #RETRYABLE_METHODS} are never replayed.
195    */
196   private RestResponse run(JsonRpcRequest request, Map<String,String> httpHeaders) throws IOException {
197      try {
198         return runOnce(request, httpHeaders);
199      } catch (IOException e) {
200         // req.run() only returns once response headers have been read, so any IOException here is pre-response.
201         if (! (isRetryableMethod(request.getMethod()) && TransportException.isStaleConnectionFailure(e)))
202            throw e;
203         return runOnce(request, httpHeaders);
204      }
205   }
206
207   private RestResponse runOnce(JsonRpcRequest request, Map<String,String> httpHeaders) throws IOException {
208      var req = restClient.post(endpoint).body(request);
209      if (httpHeaders != null) {
210         for (var e : httpHeaders.entrySet())
211            req.header(e.getKey(), e.getValue());
212      }
213      return req.run();
214   }
215
216   private static boolean isRetryableMethod(String method) {
217      return method != null && RETRYABLE_METHODS.contains(method);
218   }
219
220   /**
221    * Opens a Server-Sent-Events stream on the configured endpoint, for revision-specific facades that support a
222    * duplex (server-initiated) channel alongside the request/response {@link #send} calls.
223    *
224    * @return A reader over the opened event stream. Never <jk>null</jk>. Callers are responsible for closing it.
225    * @throws IOException If a transport-level error occurs opening the stream.
226    */
227   protected SseEventReader openEventStream() throws IOException {
228      return restClient.post(endpoint).openEventStream();
229   }
230
231   /**
232    * Opens a Server-Sent-Events stream on the configured endpoint by first POSTing {@code request} as the request
233    * body — for a revision-specific method (e.g. {@code subscriptions/listen}) whose held-open SSE response is
234    * itself the answer to one specific JSON-RPC request, as opposed to {@link #openEventStream()}'s body-less
235    * open used by the duplex server-push channel.
236    *
237    * @param request The JSON-RPC request to POST as the body that opens the stream. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
238    * @return A reader over the opened event stream. Never <jk>null</jk>. Callers are responsible for closing it.
239    * @throws IOException If a transport-level or (de)serialization error occurs opening the stream.
240    */
241   protected SseEventReader openEventStream(JsonRpcRequest request) throws IOException {
242      return openEventStream(request, Map.of());
243   }
244
245   /**
246    * Opens a Server-Sent-Events stream on the configured endpoint by first POSTing {@code request} as the request
247    * body, with additional HTTP headers on the opening request — for a revision-specific method whose held-open
248    * SSE response must agree with a header-based method/name contract (e.g. SEP-2243's {@code Mcp-Method}/
249    * {@code Mcp-Name}) the same way {@link #send(JsonRpcRequest, Map)} already does for the ordinary
250    * request/response path.
251    *
252    * <p>
253    * Unlike the body-less {@link #openEventStream()}, this opening POST is itself the answer to one specific
254    * JSON-RPC request, so the server may reject it with a JSON-RPC error envelope instead of opening the stream
255    * (e.g. a capability, {@code Accept}-header, or over-limit gate) — on any HTTP status, not just 2xx. Rather
256    * than handing that envelope to an {@link SseEventReader} (which would see zero events and eventually look
257    * like an indistinguishable transport failure), this checks the response {@code Content-Type} first: only a
258    * body reporting {@code text/event-stream} is opened as a stream. Anything else is parsed as a
259    * {@link JsonRpcResponse}; a non-<jk>null</jk> {@link JsonRpcResponse#getError() error} is thrown synchronously
260    * as an {@link McpException} carrying the server's code/message/data, matching the way mid-stream JSON-RPC
261    * errors are already surfaced to a stream's listener. A response that is neither {@code text/event-stream} nor
262    * a JSON-RPC error envelope still fails as a plain {@link IOException} (or the underlying
263    * {@link RestCallException} from a non-2xx status), never silently masquerading as an opened stream.
264    *
265    * @param request The JSON-RPC request to POST as the body that opens the stream. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
266    * @param httpHeaders Optional additional HTTP headers to add on this request. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
267    * @return A reader over the opened event stream. Never <jk>null</jk>. Callers are responsible for closing it.
268    * @throws IOException If a transport-level or (de)serialization error occurs opening the stream, or the
269    *    response was neither an SSE stream nor a JSON-RPC error envelope.
270    * @throws McpException If the server rejected {@code request} with a JSON-RPC error instead of opening the
271    *    stream.
272    */
273   protected SseEventReader openEventStream(JsonRpcRequest request, Map<String,String> httpHeaders) throws IOException {
274      reqnn("request", request);
275      var req = restClient.post(endpoint).body(request);
276      if (httpHeaders != null) {
277         for (var e : httpHeaders.entrySet())
278            req.header(e.getKey(), e.getValue());
279      }
280      if (! req.hasHeader("Accept"))
281         req.header("Accept", "text/event-stream");
282      var res = req.run();
283      var opened = false;
284      try {
285         if (isEventStream(res)) {
286            res.assertOk();
287            var r = res.body().asEventStream();
288            opened = true;
289            return r;
290         }
291         var parsed = res.body().as(JsonRpcResponse.class);
292         if (parsed != null && parsed.getError() != null)
293            throw McpException.fromJsonRpcError(parsed.getError());
294         res.assertOk(); // not a JSON-RPC error envelope either: fall back to the ordinary status diagnostic
295         throw ioex("Expected a text/event-stream response opening %s, but got Content-Type '%s'.",
296            request.getMethod(), contentTypeOf(res));
297      } finally {
298         if (! opened)
299            quiet(res::close);
300      }
301   }
302
303   private static boolean isEventStream(RestResponse res) {
304      var contentType = contentTypeOf(res);
305      return contentType != null && contentType.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT).contains("text/event-stream");
306   }
307
308   private static String contentTypeOf(RestResponse res) {
309      var h = res.getFirstHeader("Content-Type");
310      return h == null ? null : h.value();
311   }
312
313   @Override /* Overridden from Closeable */
314   public void close() throws IOException {
315      restClient.close();
316   }
317

319   // Builder
320   // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
321
322   /**
323    * Fluent, self-typed builder for {@link AbstractMcpClient} subclasses.
324    *
325    * @param <SELF> The concrete builder type (CRTP self-type), allowing dated adapters to add their own builder
326    *    methods while preserving fluent chaining.
327    * @since 10.0.0
328    */
329   @SuppressWarnings({
330      "java:S119" // 'SELF' (CRTP self-type) is intentional and clearer than a single-letter name.
331   })
332   public abstract static class Builder<SELF extends Builder<SELF>> {
333
334      String endpoint;
335      RestClient.Builder restClientBuilder = RestClient.builder();
336
337      /**
338       * Sets the MCP server endpoint URL.
339       *
340       * @param value The absolute endpoint URL (e.g. {@code "http://localhost:8080/mcp"}). Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
341       * @return This object.
342       */
343      public SELF endpoint(String value) {
344         endpoint = reqnb("endpoint", value);
345         return self();
346      }
347
348      /**
349       * Sets the HTTP transport used by the underlying {@link RestClient}.
350       *
351       * @param value The transport. Can be <jk>null</jk> (a transport is auto-discovered via {@link java.util.ServiceLoader}).
352       * @return This object.
353       */
354      public SELF transport(HttpTransport value) {
355         restClientBuilder.transport(value);
356         return self();
357      }
358
359      /**
360       * Adds a lifecycle interceptor (e.g. the auth-token seam) to the underlying {@link RestClient}.
361       *
362       * @param value The interceptor to add. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
363       * @return This object.
364       */
365      public SELF interceptor(RestCallInterceptor value) {
366         restClientBuilder.interceptors(reqnn("interceptor", value));
367         return self();
368      }
369
370      @SuppressWarnings({
371         "unchecked" // SELF is always the concrete builder subtype by construction (CRTP).
372      })
373      protected SELF self() {
374         return (SELF) this;
375      }
376   }
377}
